text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "Verified against the code: notifications/sms.py::delivery_status() reads data/sms_status.json exactly as R4/R6 state; data/sms_status.json marks exactly the 9 ids listed (SMS-00001, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16) as 'failed' and the other 7 as 'delivered'; data/outbox/sms.jsonl lines have the keys id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at, and the failed ids map to the households listed in R6. queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) does build and append the full new record itself (new id via next_number, phone from the registry, rendered text, queued_at from now()), so calling it per failed outbox record re-sends the same message to the same household without editing or removing existing outbox lines (store has no edit/delete for append-only files, per core/store.py). store.read_jsonl('outbox/sms.jsonl') is correct. The sys.path.insert pattern and docstring requirement match scripts/stock_report.py and R9. Skipping records whose status is 'delivered' or missing ensures no delivered household is texted and each failed household gets exactly one new text. The step would correctly accomplish the ticket."}}
reasoning:
Verify the plan step against code.

- delivery_status() reads data/sms_status.json — confirmed.
- 9 failed ids match: SMS-00001, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16 — confirmed.
- queue_sms builds full record and appends — confirmed. It takes household_id, template_id, params — matches outbox record keys.
- store.read_jsonl('outbox/sms.jsonl') — confirmed.
- sys.path insert per R9 — confirmed pattern.
- Docstring must state it sends SMS — per R9, correct.
- One concern: queue_sms checks household.sms_ok — if a household hasn't agreed to SMS, it would raise. But these households originally received SMS, so presumably sms_ok. Not a contradiction.
- New messages get new ids via next_number — fine.
- Plan says "Do not queue anything for records whose status is 'delivered' or missing" — correct.

Everything checks out. Accept.
